headline: 6 Bittensor-native identities catalogued (subnet owner coldkey/hotkey, validator hotkey, 3 GitHub repos); no EVM contract addresses exist — protocol runs entirely on Bittensor Substrate, outside DeFiPunkd on-chain read coverage.

findings.text: D1: Bittensor-native chain — no EVM block explorer (Etherscan/Arbiscan/etc.) applies. bittensor.ai subnet page for SN64 surfaced: owner coldkey 5FRYKhbmfXPDoHdUUDMx27E3HuMvAzwjzFMMq3rNurUhAyS9, owner hotkey 5CS3g6nVJM6ouns8n9buN9CzFf2C1YDHVcVGRcxoirKs2xbV, owner cut 18%, subnet registered at block 4,531,295. Ownership transferred at block 6,890,337.

D2: No dedicated 'deployed contracts' doc found at chutes.ai/docs. The docs site covers SDK, API reference, miner setup, and model guides but lists no on-chain address registry. protocol_metadata.deployed_contracts_doc set to null.

D3: No audit_links provided in protocol context. GitHub org contains a repo named 'chutes-audit' (auditing scripts for lite validators), but this is operational tooling, not a security audit report. No security audit PDF found.

D4: GitHub org chutesai has 51 repos. Key repos: chutes (SDK/CLI, MIT), chutes-api (validator/API backend, MIT), chutes-miner (miner stack, no license shown), fiber (Python, 29 stars), e2ee-proxy (Lua, end-to-end encryption proxy), sek8s (secure k8s with TEE). The chutes-api README explicitly names the primary validator hotkey: 5Dt7HZ7Zpw4DppPxFM7Ke3Cm7sDAWhsZXmM5ZAmE7dSVJbcQ. No Foundry broadcast files, hardhat deployments, or Solidity deployment artifacts found despite Solidity appearing in GitHub language list — likely upstream forks or peripheral code.

D5: Protocol runs on Bittensor only (single chain). No multi-chain enumeration needed. Bittensor uses Substrate/SS58 addresses, not EVM 0x addresses. DeFiPunkd read API does not support Bittensor chainId.

D6: No factory contracts applicable. Protocol is a Bittensor subnet with off-chain validator/miner infrastructure; no factory pattern in EVM sense. Subnet metagraph manages neuron slots (256/256 filled). Not applicable.

D7: Role taxonomy applied. Three principal Bittensor identities: (1) subnet owner coldkey — controls subnet registration, owner cut, and ownership transfers; (2) subnet owner hotkey — operational signing for subnet owner functions (updated at block 8,576,465); (3) primary validator hotkey — routes requests, sets weights, manages miner billing and incentive distribution. All are SS58 Substrate keypairs, not EVM addresses. actor_class set to 'unknown' as Bittensor key type has no direct mapping to EVM multisig/EOA taxonomy.

D8: All three Bittensor addresses in admin_addresses trace to fetched URLs: owner coldkey and owner hotkey from bittensor.ai/subnets/64; validator hotkey from github.com/chutesai/chutes-api README and chutes.ai/docs/miner-resources/overview. Note: SS58 addresses cannot be placed in the 0x-format address field required by the schema — they are recorded in role field descriptions and evidence[].shows instead.

rationale.verdict: Discovery run walked chutes.ai website, chutes.ai/docs, github.com/chutesai org (51 repos), github.com/chutesai/chutes-api README, bittensor.ai/subnets/64, and chutes.ai/docs/miner-resources/overview. Three on-chain Bittensor identities and three primary GitHub repos catalogued. No EVM contract addresses exist or are discoverable — the protocol runs entirely on Bittensor Substrate using SS58 keypairs, outside DeFiPunkd's supported chainId set. grade=unknown because the DeFiPunkd on-chain read API cannot verify Bittensor-native state, and no EVM addresses were found to surface.

evidence.shows: Official website confirms Chutes is a decentralized serverless AI compute platform powered by Bittensor, GitHub link points to github.com/chutesai, support email support@chutes.ai confirmed.

GitHub org 'Chutes Global Corp' with 51 repos including chutes (SDK/CLI), chutes-api (validator/API), chutes-miner, fiber, e2ee-proxy, sek8s. Languages include Python, Rust, Lua, Solidity (likely forks). Org has no public members listed.
Developer documentation site. Covers SDK, API reference, miner resources, model guides. No deployed contracts address page found. Contact options: support@chutes.ai, Discord discord.gg/chutes.

Validator/API backend repo (MIT license). README explicitly states primary validator hotkey is 5Dt7HZ7Zpw4DppPxFM7Ke3Cm7sDAWhsZXmM5ZAmE7dSVJbcQ. Describes operator-run Kubernetes/Ansible infrastructure. No EVM contract addresses. Repo has 28 stars, 17 forks, 1252 commits on main.

Subnet SN64 on-chain identity: owner coldkey 5FRYKhbmfXPDoHdUUDMx27E3HuMvAzwjzFMMq3rNurUhAyS9, owner hotkey 5CS3g6nVJM6ouns8n9buN9CzFf2C1YDHVcVGRcxoirKs2xbV, owner cut 18%, 256/256 neurons, tempo 360 blocks, subnet registered block 4531295, ownership transferred block 6890337 to current owner, SubnetOwnerHotkeySet at block 8576465 (3 months ago). Operated by Chutes Global Corp, IBC registered in Nevis, registration C 61974.

Miner setup docs confirm validator hotkey 5Dt7HZ7Zpw4DppPxFM7Ke3Cm7sDAWhsZXmM5ZAmE7dSVJbcQ as the supported/primary validator; api endpoint api.chutes.ai; registry registry.chutes.ai; socket wss://ws.chutes.ai. Miners register on netuid 64.

D2: No deployed contracts address doc found at chutes.ai/docs or linked from website; protocol has no EVM contracts to list
D3: No security audit report found; chutes-audit GitHub repo is validator tooling, not an external security audit

D4: Solidity language appears in GitHub org language list but no deployment artifacts (broadcast/, deployments/, addresses.json) found in chutes-api or chutes repos; likely from upstream forks (e.g. llama.cpp, codex); commit SHAs not pinned because no deployment artifacts were located

protocol_metadata.about: Chutes is a decentralized serverless AI compute platform operating as Subnet 64 (SN64) on the Bittensor network, developed by Rayon Labs (trading as Chutes Global Corp). Developers deploy containerized AI applications ('chutes') written as FastAPI-style Python code, which are routed by validators to a network of GPU-contributing miners and executed in isolated Docker containers. GPU hardware authenticity is cryptographically enforced by GraVal middleware, which performs VRAM capacity checks, matrix multiplications, and device challenges as middleware within each running container. Users pay only for verified compute time, accessing models via an OpenAI-compatible API endpoint (llm.chutes.ai), with billing and incentives managed through Bittensor hotkey signatures and TAO token emissions.
